topic.name: The Four Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text: Let $A$ be a $m \times n$ matrix. What is the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $A?$
question.explanation:
Pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ by $A$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A{:}$

\[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \\ a_1 & a_2 & \cdots & a_n \\ \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \end{bmatrix}}_{\large A} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ \vdots \\ x_n \end{bmatrix}}_{\large \mathbf{x}} = x_1 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_1 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_2 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} +\cdots+ x_n \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_n \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} \]

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $A$ must be $\text{Col}(A),$ the column space of $A.$

example.title: Identifying the Images of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of the Matrix Under Its Action

question.text:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}(A)$ for every matrix $A?$

  1. $\text{Col}(A^T)$
  2. $\text{Null}(A^T)$
  3. $\text{Null}(A)$
question.explanation:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ consists of all linear combinations of the columns of $A$, that is, the rows of $A^T.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of $A^T,$ it must be orthogonal to each row of $A^T.$ But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by $A^T,$ we actually multiply each row of $A^T$ by that vector. So, $\text{Col}(A)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $A,$ which is $\text{Null}(A^T).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

Note: In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

example.title: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}(B)$ for every matrix $B?$

  1. $\text{Null}(B^T)$
  2. $\text{Col}(B)$
  3. $\text{Col}(B^T)$
question.explanation:
Recall that $\text{Null}(B)$ contains all vectors that, when pre-multiplied by $B,$ result in the zero-vector $\mathbf{0}.$

When pre-multiplying a vector by $B,$ we actually multiply each row of $B$ by that vector. So, $\text{Null}(B)$ must be orthogonal to the row space of $B,$ which is $\text{Col}(A^T).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

Note: In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $B$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

example.title: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}(B^T)$ for every matrix $B?$

  1. $\text{Null}(B)$
  2. $\text{Col}(B)$
  3. $\text{Col}(B^T)$
question.explanation:
Recall that $\text{Null}(B^T)$ is the left null space of $B.$ This consists of vectors that, when pre-multiplied by $B^T,$ result in the zero-vector $\mathbf{0}.$

When pre-multiplying a vector by $B^T,$ we actually multiply each row of $B^T$, that is, each column of $B$, by that vector. So, $\text{Null}(B^T)$ must be orthogonal to the column space of $B,$ which is $\text{Col}(B).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

example.title: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}(XY)$ for all compatible matrices $X$ and $Y?$

  1. $\text{Null}(Y^T \! X^T)$
  2. $\text{Col}(Y^T \! X^T)$
  3. $\text{Null}(XY)$
question.explanation:
Recall that $\text{Col}(XY)$ consists of all linear combinations of the columns of $XY$, that is, the rows of $(XY)^T = Y^T \! X^T.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of $Y^T \! X^T,$ it must be orthogonal to each row of $Y^T \! X^T.$ But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by $Y^T \! X^T,$ we actually multiply each row of $Y^T \! X^T$ by that vector. So, $\text{Col}(XY)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $XY,$ which is $\text{Null}(Y^T \! X^T).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
